llm.summary: This skill connects an agent to mailbox.bot to send and manage postal mail, and the risky capabilities are disclosed and bounded by sandbox keys, pricing checks, cost caps, and human approval flows.

dimensions.detail: Remote network access and document/mail transmission are expected for a postal-mail API, and the artifact documents sandbox keys, dry runs, real price previews, and no-charge/no-physical-mail sandbox behavior.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation config connects to a remote MCP server with bearer authentication; no local executable payload is shipped, aside from an optional mcp-remote bridge command for clients that require one.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The main SKILL.md gives usage cases and operational safeguards such as previewing costs, treating OCR/mail content as untrusted, reading current state before mutation, and requiring owner approval for inbound scan/forward/discard actions; the server metadata is broader but not deceptive.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill uses persistent remote account state, API keys, mailbox records, webhooks, and prepaid credits, but it does not install local persistence, modify tools, access payment cards, or claim privilege beyond the mailbox.bot account scope.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose is high-impact because it can send physical mail, handle legal/certified mail, read inbound postal context, and propose mailbox actions, but those capabilities match the stated postal-mail service purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, treat this as a real postal-mail and mailbox service: use a sandbox key first, keep API keys out of logs and prompts, require explicit human confirmation for live sends or legal/certified mail, and review costs, document previews, and mailbox actions before approval.
llm.findings:
[TM1] expected: The flagged DELETE endpoint is a documented cancellation API for queued outbound mail; it is purpose-aligned and constrained to mail still in submitted status.
[E1] expected: The flagged curl examples read inbound mailbox items from mailbox.bot using the configured API key; this is sensitive data access, but it is the advertised mailbox-context function rather than hidden exfiltration.
[SQP-2] expected: The install guide could be more prominent about real-world costs and document transmission, but it does disclose a remote MCP server, outbound physical mail, inbound mail context, and sandbox test keys.
[SQP-1] expected: The server description is broad and includes legal/business mail workflows, but the main skill instructions add usage examples, dry-run/cost controls, and approval guidance sufficient for a benign classification.
